'''Bernard Teissier''' ({{IPA|fr|tɛsje}}; born 1945)<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=bigQvHvkF_YC&hl= ''Plane algebraic curves''] by Gerd Fischer, American Mathematical Soc., 2001, p. 229</ref>  is a French [[mathematician]] and a member of the [[Nicolas Bourbaki]] group. He has made major contributions to [[algebraic geometry]] and [[commutative algebra]], specifically to [[singularity theory]], [[multiplicity theory]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://indico.math.cnrs.fr/event/202/contributions/967/attachments/562/615/2015-Popescu-Pampu-Aussois.pdf|format=PDF|title=How Teissier mixed multiplicities|author=Patrick Popescu-Pampu|website=Indico.math.cnrs.fr|access-date=7 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://indico.math.cnrs.fr/event/202/contributions/954/attachments/558/611/2015-Gaffney-Ausois.pdf|format=PDF|title=Families of Isolated Singularities and Three Inspirations from Bernard Teissier|author=Terence Gaffney|website=Indico.math.cnrs.fr|access-date=7 March 2022}}</ref> and [[valuation theory]].

Teissier attained his [[doctorate]] from [[Paris Diderot University]] in 1973, under supervision of [[Heisuke Hironaka]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=13781}}</ref> He was a member and a leading figure of [[Nicolas Bourbaki]].<ref>{{citation|title=Bourbaki: a secret society of mathematicians|first=Maurice|last=Mashaal|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|year=2006|page=18|isbn=978-0-8218-3967-6|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-CXn6y_1nJ8C&pg=PA18}}.</ref> Along with [[Alain Connes]], he gave the 1975/1976 [[Peccot Lectures]]. He was an invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematics at Warsaw in 1983.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=International Mathematical Union (IMU)|website=Mathunion.org|access-date=7 March 2022|archive-date=24 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, Ams.org, retrieved 2013-08-25.</ref>
